title: The Cloud of Unknowing (14th century)
hookLine: an anonymous English guide: God is reached by love, not by thinking

lines: YOU CAN'T THINK YOUR WAY INTO LOVE.
cards: A swimming manual has never kept anyone afloat. A list of reasons to love someone is not the love. Some things can't be reached by thinking.

Somewhere in England, in the 1300s, a writer with no name sat down to teach a young person how to pray, and made exactly this point about God. The book is short, strange, and funny in places. Its title gives today's word.

teach.b: The Cloud of Unknowing was written in Middle English, the English of Chaucer's time, by an author who hid his name on purpose. Some readers guess he was a priest, perhaps a Carthusian monk. Nobody knows.
First, the two clouds. When you turn toward God, he says, you find a darkness between you and God, a cloud of unknowing, that your mind can't get through.
So you put all your thoughts, even good ones, beneath you in a cloud of forgetting. Second, the key. God can't be reached by thinking, he says, but God can be reached by love.
He puts it in two halves: by love God may be gotten and held, but by thought never. The mind can know about God. Only love can touch God.

teach.h: A SHARP DART OF LONGING LOVE.
teach.b: In the cloud, you send up what he calls a sharp dart of longing love. Keep it short: one word, even one syllable, like God, or love, fastened to your heart. A short prayer, he says, pierces heaven.
His picture: someone whose house is on fire doesn't make a speech. They shout one word: fire. Fourth, the humor.
He warns against people who strain so hard at prayer that they pull strange faces and twist themselves about. Relax, he says.
These last two weeks walked through ways of praying: contemplation, lectio divina, the examen, imagination, the Hours, Compline, the Jesus Prayer, a kitchen, a sacred word, and now a cloud.
Tomorrow, a saint builds a castle.

how: Some Catholics read The Cloud of Unknowing as a guide to silent, wordless prayer, repeating a single short word like God or love as a movement of the heart, and it underlies modern methods such as centering prayer.

o: doubting whether God is there at all, and staying unsure
forgetting what you learned so faith can stay simple
the dark between you and God that only love gets through

games.q: what's inside the book — tap the pairs.

s: we know who wrote The Cloud of Unknowing
the author hid his name. some guess he was a priest, perhaps a Carthusian, but nobody knows.
the book says God can be reached by love, not by thought
the mind can know about God; only love can touch God.
the book says to strain hard in prayer
it warns against straining, and pokes fun at people who pull strange faces as they pray.

games.q: you're sitting in prayer, and all you find is darkness, a cloud your mind can't get through. what does the book say to do?
o: give up; this prayer isn't for you.
send up a short dart of longing love.
games.why: love, not thought, gets through the cloud. keep it short: one word, even one syllable.

practice: Let your thoughts drift down beneath you, even the good ones. If you pray, choose one word, God or love, and send it upward, short and whole, whenever you feel the pull, with no explaining.
If you don't pray, send the word toward whatever you love most, and let the word do the loving.

wordCard.voice: Unknowing. The darkness between you and God that thinking can't get through, taught by an anonymous English guide from the 1300s who said God can be held only by love. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: by love, not thought. Two weeks of ways of praying, done.
